name: Luna 9 landing capsule

location.name: Oceanus Procellarum, west of the craters Reiner and Marius (reported site)

headline: The first soft landing on another world, and the first photos from the Moon's surface
story: On 3 February 1966, a small Soviet capsule came to rest in the Ocean of Storms. It rolled upright and unfolded four spring-loaded petals to steady itself. For the first time, something built on Earth had landed gently on another world.

A camera with a turning mirror swept the horizon and sent home panoramas of grey ground and nearby rocks: the first pictures ever taken from the lunar surface. They showed the ground could bear a lander's weight without sinking into dust. The signals continued until 6 February, when the batteries ran out.

The capsule is still out there, somewhere west of the craters Reiner and Marius. Its exact resting place has never been confirmed: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has found no sign of it at the reported coordinates.
